items.title: Romania receives first two modernized IAR-99 jet trainers for F-16 pilots
items.summary:
Romania’s Ministry of National Defense (MApN) has accepted the first two of 10 IAR-99 SM jet trainers modernized by state-owned aircraft manufacturer Avioane Craiova. The aircraft were handed over in Craiova on November 16, 2026, more than two years after the original delivery deadline. 

The handover was confirmed in a statement issued by the ministry . The upgraded aircraft will support advanced jet training, particularly the transition to the F-16 fighter, while retaining a secondary close air support capability. 

They will be operated at the Air Force Application School “Aurel Vlaicu” in Boboc, where between 25 and 40 pilots are expected to undergo training annually in preparation for the F-16, depending on the number of graduates from the “Henri Coandă” Air Force Academy. 

IAR-99 modernization program faces delivery delays 

A Romanian Air Force IAR-99 Șoim jet trainer at the Avioane Craiova factory. (Credit: Romanian Government) 

The IAR-99 is a Romanian-designed, twin-seat subsonic jet trainer and light attack aircraft developed during the 1980s and manufactured by Avioane Craiova. The prototype made its first flight in December 1985, and the type entered Romanian Air Force service in 1988. 

A subsequent modernization produced the IAR-99 Șoim (Hawk), adapted for training pilots transitioning to the MiG-21 LanceR. 

The modernization to the SM (Standard Modernizat) configuration includes upgraded avionics, a new weapons system, and maintenance work to extend the airframes’ service lives. 

The contract, worth 275 million lei (approximately $57 million) excluding…
items.t: Romania receives first two modernized IAR-99 jet trainers for F-16 pilots

items.title: RTX’s Collins Aerospace begins work on new propeller MRO facility in India
items.summary:
RTX’s Collins Aerospace has officially begun construction work on a new propeller maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) facility in India.

On November 17, 2026, the US-company announced that the first spades were in the ground at the already established 26-acre Collins India Operations Center (CIOC) in Bengaluru.

Scheduled to open in early 2029, the new facility will specialize in advanced propeller systems for ATR 42/72 regional aircraft and Airbus C295 military transport platforms throughout the Asia Pacific region.

According to Collins Aerospace, the center is the country’s first propeller MRO facility authorized by a foreign aerospace original equipment manufacturer.

Collins Aerospace 

India is expected to become the third-largest civil aviation market in the world by 2035, behind only the United States and China.

“As regional connectivity expands across India, maintaining high fleet availability for operators is critical,” said Ajay Mahajan, President of Advanced Structures, Collins Aerospace. “By establishing in-country propeller MRO capabilities, we are bringing world-class aftermarket expertise directly to our customers, reducing turnaround times and operational downtime. Support from the government of Karnataka has helped enable this investment.”

Collins Aerospace said that over the last five years it has invested more than $200 million to help establish aerospace services in India including engineering, manufacturing, testing and specialized aftermarket propeller maintenance.

Collins India Operations Center opened in 2025 and supports the production of…
items.t: RTX’s Collins Aerospace begins work on new propeller MRO facility in India

items.title: Ghana Air Force takes delivery of Dassault Falcon 6X executive jet
items.summary:
The Ghana Air Force has taken delivery of a Dassault Falcon 6X long-range business jet intended for executive transport. 

The aircraft arrived at Accra International Airport (ACC) on November 16, 2026, the service said in a statement . 

The jet received a water cannon salute on arrival. Defense Minister Kenneth Gilbert Adjei, French Ambassador to Ghana Diarra Dimé Labille and members of the Ghana Armed Forces’ military high command attended the reception. 

Ghana approved Falcon 6X alongside four Airbus helicopters 

The Falcon 6X was purchased under one of two procurement agreements presented by Deputy Defense Minister Ernest Brogya Genfi approved by Ghana’s Parliament on December 4, 2025. 

The first was a $60.68 million sale and purchase agreement with Dassault Aviation for one Falcon 6X. The second was a €125.97 million contract with Airbus Helicopters for one H160 and three H175 helicopters. 

Presenting the report, James Agalga, chairman of Parliament’s Committee on Defense and Interior, said the Ghana Air Force could no longer afford to rely on its aging Mi-17 helicopters and Falcon 900EX executive jet. The committee estimated that, over 15 years, the new fleet would cost 30% to 40% less to own and operate than the aircraft it replaces. 

Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson had outlined the broader fleet renewal program in the 2026 budget statement on November 13, 2025, including plans to acquire four helicopters and two fixed-wing aircraft. The announcement followed the crash of a Ghana Air Force Z-9 helicopter in the Ashanti region on August 6, 2025, which…
items.t: Ghana Air Force takes delivery of Dassault Falcon 6X executive jet

items.title: AAPA urges governments to rethink airline taxes, fees amid soaring fuel costs
items.summary:
Asia Pacific airlines are filling more seats than ever, but soaring fuel prices are eating into the returns. Now the region’s airline association wants governments to step in before the damage spreads.

At the close of its 70th Assembly of Presidents in Kuala Lumpur on November 13, 2026, the Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA) called on governments across the region to provide timely, practical support to carriers facing sharply higher fuel prices and mounting operational hurdles.

The two-day event, hosted by Malaysia Airlines and attended by AeroTime, united more than 170 delegates under the theme “Redefining Aviation: Growth, Resilience and Innovation.” It also marked a milestone for the association, which was founded in September 1966, as it celebrated its 60th anniversary this year.

“Governments must recognize these pressures and work constructively with the industry to provide support that safeguards the long-term viability of air transport across the region,” said AAPA Director General Wong Hong. 

Wong joined AAPA in April after a decade with Delta Air Lines in Shanghai and 13 years at Singapore Airlines. Kuala Lumpur was his first Assembly in the role.

AAPA Director General Wong Hong 

Record load factors, but $186-a-barrel fuel drains margins 

On the surface, demand has held up. Passenger traffic for Asia Pacific airlines grew 1.9% in the first nine months of 2026, and average load factors reached a record 83%.

“Let’s be candid. A full aircraft does not necessarily translate into a healthy bottom line!” Wong told delegates during his opening address…
items.t: AAPA urges governments to rethink airline taxes, fees amid soaring fuel costs

items.title: Airbus delivers first A321XLR aircraft to Middle East Airlines
items.summary:
Airbus has delivered the first A321XLR aircraft to Lebanese flag carrier Middle East Airlines (MEA). The handover, which occurred on November 17, 2026, took place at the European aircraft manufacturer’s facility in Finkenwerder (XFW), near Hamburg, from where the aircraft will depart on its delivery flight to Beirut’s Rafic-Hariri International Airport (BEY). 

MEA became the launch customer of the A321XLR after it was the first airline to place a firm order for the type at the Paris Air Show 2019 and was long expected to be the first airline to operate the type. However, that distinction finally went to Spanish airline Iberia, which put the longest-range version of the A321 into service in November 2024.  

The newly delivered aircraft (registration OD-XLR) is the first of five that the Lebanese carrier has on order. MEA has another 20 A320 family aircraft (10 A320s and 10 A321s) in its fleet. It also has four A330-200s for long-haul services, which are slated to be replaced before the end of 2028 by an equal number of A330-900neo aircraft it has on order. 

MEA will operate its A321XLRs with a two-class configuration with 22 fully lie-flat business class seats and 138 seats economy, for a total of 160 passengers. The aircraft also features the state-of-the-art Airbus Airspace cabin, with customizable ambient lighting and extra-large overhead bins.

The post Airbus delivers first A321XLR aircraft to Middle East Airlines  appeared first on AeroTime .
items.t: Airbus delivers first A321XLR aircraft to Middle East Airlines

items.title: Lufthansa pilot contract proposal met with union deadline threat
items.summary:
An employment proposal submitted by Lufthansa to Germany’s Vereinigung Cockpit union regarding pilots working conditions and their future security has been met with frustration.

On November 17, 2026, Lufthansa hoped that a promise of up to 1,000 new pilot hires by the end of 2033 and up to 150 additional captain promotions per year would help break a deadlock that has seen staff strike on multiple occasions this year .

The proposals were based on recommendations made by former state premiers Bodo Ramelow and Roland Koch, who were each appointed as arbitrators by one of the two sides.

Recommendations to increase the competitiveness of Lufthansa include temporary stabilization of pay levels, adjustments to salary scales, and measures to increase productivity.

Lufthansa 

Lufthansa said the variable compensation component would also be adjusted. While at the same time, the carrier is offering a one-off payment for 2027 and 2028 as well as salary increases from 2029 onwards.

For the pilots of Lufthansa CityLine, which ceased operations in April 2026, the offer includes “concrete employment prospects” such as the option of transferring to Lufthansa.

Dr. Michael Niggemann, Member of the Lufthansa Group Executive Board, said that the “recommendations show a clear path to an agreement”.

“We are ready to take this path and, on this basis, have submitted a comprehensive offer to VC,” said Niggemann. “It combines long-term employment and career prospects for our pilots with measures to strengthen the competitiveness of Lufthansa Classic. What matters now is that, together with…
items.t: Lufthansa pilot contract proposal met with union deadline threat

items.title: Why Allegiant Air Broke Boeing Loyalty For Nearly 10 Years For Exclusive Airbus Operations But Decided To Go Back
items.summary: Allegiant Air surprised the aviation industry in January 2022 when it announced an order for 50 brand-new Boeing 737 MAX aircraft, with options for another 50. The Las Vegas-based leisure carrier had spent much of the previous decade moving away from Boeing-lineage aircraft, completing its transition to an exclusively Airbus fleet in 2018. So its decision to return to Boeing represented a fundamental change in its aircraft purchasing strategy.

items.title: Australian Army receives seventh and eighth AH-64E Apaches as Tiger replacement
items.summary:
The Australian Army has taken delivery of its seventh and eighth AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, bringing its fleet to a quarter of the 29 aircraft it expects to operate by 2029.

A US Air Force C-17A Globemaster III flew the two helicopters to RAAF Base Townsville in Queensland, where they will join the Army’s 1st Aviation Regiment. 

The regiment operates two Apache squadrons and is part of the 16th Aviation Brigade, which is also home to the Army’s CH-47 Chinook cargo helicopter fleet in Townsville.

Live-fire training and field deployment 

Brigadier Fern Thompson, Commander of the 16th Aviation Brigade, said its rapid introduction had been carefully managed. “The AH-64E Apache only entered Australian Army service last year, and already we have it baring its teeth,” she said.

The Army is preparing for its second Apache live-fire activity in Townsville this year, which will certify more pilots to fire the helicopter’s 30mm gun, rockets and Hellfire missiles. During the November iteration of Exercise Possum Guns, the 1st Aviation Regiment will also test its ability to deploy the Apache from a simulated field environment.

Thompson said aircrew and maintainers had trained in the United States and the United Kingdom ahead of the deliveries, so the Army could fly and sustain the helicopters as soon as they arrived. 

“Now, only a year after the first AH-64E Apaches were delivered, we have received a quarter of our fleet and have shown we can employ them with the full range of live munitions and sensors using our own people,” she said.

Replacing the Tiger 

The Apaches…
items.t: Australian Army receives seventh and eighth AH-64E Apaches as Tiger replacement

items.title: Serbian MiG-29 fighter crashes near Belgrade, killing pilot
items.summary:
A Serbian Air Force and Air Defense MiG-29 fighter crashed near Stara Pazova, northwest of Belgrade, on November 17, 2026, killing its pilot, Major Goran Bulajić, according to Serbia’s Ministry of Defense.

The aircraft, assigned to the 204th Air Brigade, went down at around 08:45 local time, the ministry said in a statement carried by Serbian broadcaster N1 . Bulajić had served in the Serbian Armed Forces since 1996. 

The aircraft crashed in a field between Nova Pazova and Stara Pazova, according to Serbian media reports. Footage published by local outlets showed thick black smoke rising from the wreckage.

Serbian military launches investigation into MiG-29 crash 

The Ministry of Defense said it had established two commissions to investigate the accident. One will examine the circumstances of the crash and any potential responsibility within the military, while a separate Serbian Air Force and Air Defense expert commission will determine its cause.

Military police were dispatched to the site, and the relevant prosecutor was notified.

The ministry did not disclose the purpose of the flight, whether the pilot attempted to eject, or whether the crash caused any damage on the ground.

Defense Minister Bratislav Gašić and Lieutenant General Tiosav Janković, acting Chief of the General Staff and Commander of the Air Force and Air Defense, sent condolences to Bulajić’s family. Janković also traveled to the crash site.

Serbia’s MiG-29 fleet set to be replaced by Rafale fighters 

The 204th Air Brigade operates Serbia’s MiG-29 fleet from Batajnica Air Base, near Belgrade.…
items.t: Serbian MiG-29 fighter crashes near Belgrade, killing pilot

items.title: Israeli airline Arkia changes hands, new businessman owner acquires 82% stake
items.summary:
Israeli airline Arkia has a new owner after businessman Ronen Elad acquired an 82% equity stake. 

Elad will invest US$30 million in the carrier as part of a broader shareholder agreement which will also see the current majority owners, the Nakash brothers, invest a further US$8.5 million to retain a 3% stake. The airline’s staff will see their stake drop from 22 to 15%, although they will retain pre-existent veto rights over certain decisions. 

Securing staff agreements was one of the cornerstones of the deal. Arkia workers had rejected earlier attempts to take over the company by at least two competing investor groups. 

Arkia had been in play for quite some time and among those that expressed interest in acquiring the airline was its direct competitor, Israir , the country’s second largest airline.  

The final acquirer, Ronen Elad, has interests in multiple industries, from electronics to defense and consumer goods, and it is known for his expertise in acquiring and turning around existing businesses. 

Arkia’s finances will be propped up by an additional US$7.8 million, which the Israeli state will provide to compensate for disruption caused by the recent military confrontation with Iran. 

The extra funds will be a lifeline for Arkia, which is reported to be going through a challenging financial situation. Israeli media have estimated that its losses for the first half of the year amount to around US$30 million, a figure that may double by the end of the year. For reference, Arkia posted a profit of approximately US$20 million in 2024. 

As of November 2026, Arkia…
items.t: Israeli airline Arkia changes hands, new businessman owner acquires 82% stake

items.title: Elroy Air signs deal with UAE firm for up to 20 hybrid-electric cargo drones
items.summary:
US-based Elroy Air has signed an agreement with Barq Group for up to 20 autonomous hybrid-electric cargo drones, designed to be used for defense and commercial logistics missions.

On November 16, 2026, Elroy Air and Abu Dhabi’s Barq Group said the contract initially covered a $10.25 million deposit covering five firm orders, as well as an additional 15 deposit-backed production slot reservations.

Named Chaparral, the autonomous heavy-cargo drone can carry more than 500 pounds over a range of up to 450 miles and does not rely on designated runways for takeoff and landing.

Under the agreement terms, Barq Group has made a binding commitment for the five firm-order aircraft and will fund 50% of the price of each firm-order Chaparral through its initial deposit, with additional pre-delivery payments to support the production slot reservations.

Elroy Air 

The purchase agreement for up to 20 Chaparral cargo drones represents a total initial transaction value of up to $70 million for the aircraft alone. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in 2027.

“The Middle East and North Africa region is one of the most dynamic logistics markets in the world, and Barq Group is leading its shift toward smart, autonomous mobility,” Elroy Air CEO, Andrew Clare, said. “Our agreement marks a major step in expanding Chaparral’s reach globally, and together with Barq Group, we will advance how autonomous aircraft can move critical cargo across long distances and challenging terrain faster and more efficiently than conventional platforms.”

Kratos Defense & Security Solutions will build the…
items.t: Elroy Air signs deal with UAE firm for up to 20 hybrid-electric cargo drones

items.title: ICEYE launches takeover bid for Italy’s rocket maker Avio
items.summary:
Finnish satellite operator ICEYE has launched an all-cash takeover bid for Avio, the Italian manufacturer of the Vega-C rocket and solid rocket motors for European missiles, in a deal valued at approximately €2.05 billion. 

ICEYE announced the offer on November 17, 2026, through Iris 2 S.p.A., an indirect wholly owned Italian subsidiary. It is offering €41 per share, a 21.3% premium to Avio’s official share price of €33.79 on November 16, 2026. The formal offer notice puts the maximum payment at €2,052,657,251. 

Avio said on November 17, 2026, that its board would begin evaluating the offer, which aims to delist the company from Euronext STAR Milan. 

ICEYE seeks to combine satellite intelligence with European rocket launch capabilities 

ICEYE says the acquisition would create a vertically integrated European space and defense company, combining Avio’s launch and propulsion capabilities with its own satellite manufacturing, constellation operations and intelligence services. It also argues the deal would support more frequent Vega launches. 

Avio is the prime contractor for Vega-C, Europe’s light-lift launcher, and co-produces the P120C solid rocket motor used by both Vega-C and Ariane 6 through Europropulsion, its joint venture with ArianeGroup. It also supplies propulsion for the Aster and CAMM-ER missile families. 

Artist’s rendering of an ICEYE synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite in orbit. (Credit: ICEYE) 

ICEYE operates a constellation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites, four of which launched aboard SpaceX’s Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission in…
items.t: ICEYE launches takeover bid for Italy’s rocket maker Avio

items.title: Ryanair to invest €500 million in new engine shop in Seville, Spain
items.summary:
Irish low-cost carrier Ryanair is set to invest €500 million to set up a new maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) center in Seville, Spain. 

The new facility will focus on jet engine maintenance and repair and will be located at Puerto de Sevilla, an inland port on the Guadalquivir River, which is connected to the Atlantic Ocean. 

Both the Andalusian regional government and the Spanish government will support the project financially, with an investment of €24 million and €17 million, respectively. The new facility is expected to create around 600 jobs in an area with relatively high unemployment. 

The Andalusian capital has reportedly beaten 12 other cities which were also vying to receive this investment. 

The new facility will also strengthen Seville’s credentials as a major aerospace manufacturing hub. The city is already a production center for Airbus and is host to the final assembly lines for the Airbus A400M and C295 military aircraft as well as several Tier 1 suppliers. A new MRO and conversion center for A330 MRTT aircraft is also expected to open in the city in 2027. 

Ryanair’s decision was confirmed on November 16, 2026, on the same day that the Irish carrier opened another MRO facility in the Iberian Peninsula, this time in Porto, in northern Portugal. 

The Porto MRO center is a 4,900 square-meter facility featuring a two-bay line maintenance hangar and dedicated component workshops. The Irish low-cost carrier has invested around €40 million in this facility, which is expected to create 150 jobs locally and service the approximately 30 aircraft it…
items.t: Ryanair to invest €500 million in new engine shop in Seville, Spain

items.title: Russia halts all Crimean Bridge traffic after second air strike in two days
items.summary:
Russia suspended road and rail traffic across the Crimean Bridge on November 17, 2026, following a second overnight attack in as many days, as footage emerged appearing to show the road bridge’s main arch had collapsed into the Kerch Strait.

In a statement published at 08:51 Moscow time , Russia’s Ministry of Transport attributed the disruption to another drone attack. It said specialists were assessing the damage and reported no casualties on the bridge, according to preliminary information.

Motorists were advised not to travel toward the crossing. The ministry did not describe the extent of the damage or provide a timeline for reopening.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of occupied Crimea, had reported the attack at 01:35 Moscow time . He later said two people had been killed in a drone attack in the peninsula’s Leninsky district, without establishing whether the deaths were directly connected to the bridge strike.

Footage suggests Crimean Bridge road arch has collapsed 

Video and photographs published on November 17, 2026, appear to show the steel arch over the road bridge’s navigation span missing, with part of the roadway in the Kerch Strait. The parallel railway arch appears to remain standing. Russian authorities have not confirmed a collapse.

Footage showing the destruction of the road arch and span of the Crimean Bridge across the Kerch Strait.

Unlike an ordinary bridge span, the massive steel arch cannot be easily replaced. Road traffic across the bridge has been completely severed, leaving the occupied land corridor as the only remaining…
items.t: Russia halts all Crimean Bridge traffic after second air strike in two days

items.title: United outage delays departures as pilots lose access to aircraft weight data
items.summary:
A United Airlines computer outage delayed departures on November 16, 2026, after pilots lost access to the final aircraft weights they needed to calculate takeoff performance. United said it resolved the problem around 6 p.m. Eastern time. Flights already in the air and those operated by United Express continued unaffected.

Several applications used by United pilots went down, including crew messaging, according to an Air Line Pilots Association memo. The outage made it impossible for the airline to provide outbound flights with final weights, the union told pilots. Crews use the aircraft’s weight, along with runway and weather conditions, to determine whether they can safely take off.

The union advised crews to check with local United staff before pushing back. In Houston, one United pilot asked the tower for permission to stay at the gate until the system came back online. About an hour and 40 minutes passed between the first pilot reports and the fix. United said it had no indication of a cybersecurity incident, but it did not say what caused the outage.

By 6:50 p.m. Eastern time, FlightAware had recorded 645 United flights delayed, about 20% of its Monday schedule, and 25 cancellations.

United’s outage came three days after a failure in the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) telecommunications network forced the agency to halt departures across the country for more than four hours. On Sunday, United CEO Scott Kirby had called for greater investment in backup systems for US air traffic control.

United experienced a similar disruption in August 2025 , when a…
items.t: United outage delays departures as pilots lose access to aircraft weight data

items.title: Citing loss-of-control risk, EASA orders additional ATR de-icing system checks
items.summary:
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has ordered operators of ATR 42 and ATR 72 turboprops to check their de-icing systems as often as every 160 flight hours, warning that a valve failure could go undetected until an aircraft encounters icing and lead to an unrecoverable loss of control.

The airworthiness directive, issued November 16, 2026, takes effect November 30. EASA had already shortened the time between checks in January 2025 after a design review identified the risk. A subsequent analysis of how the valves could fail prompted ATR to revise its maintenance instructions again in October.

Brazilian investigators identified ice buildup and multiple de-icing system failures among the factors that contributed to the August 9, 2024, crash of Voepass Flight 2283 . All 62 people aboard the ATR 72-500 died when it crashed in Vinhedo, Brazil. ATR issued its first notice to operators about the valve checks in October 2024, about two months after the accident.

The order covers the valves that regulate pressure and shut off the air supply to the de-icing system. How often operators must test them depends on the aircraft model and whether ATR modified it at the factory or an operator had the work done later.

The biggest change is for modified ATR 42-400s, ATR 42-500s and ATR 72s. Under the January 2025 order, those aircraft could fly up to 1,050 hours between checks. The new limit is 160 hours, an 85% reduction. For aircraft of the same models without the modification, the interval drops from 700 hours to 210. Operators of the earlier ATR 42-200, -300 and -320…
items.t: Citing loss-of-control risk, EASA orders additional ATR de-icing system checks

items.title: Azul puts its first Cessna SkyCourier to work flying oil crews in the Amazon
items.summary:
Azul Conecta has put its first Cessna SkyCourier to work flying oil crews for Petrobras in the Brazilian Amazon. The regional airline also plans to sell seats on the weekly flights that bring the 19-seat turboprop back to Manaus and return it to the oilfields.

The aircraft, registered PS-ENE, arrived in Brazil recently and entered service on November 3, 2026. Azul won a four-year contract to transport workers for the Brazilian oil company, whose operations in the state of Amazonas include the oil and gas fields at Porto Urucu.

Under the schedule Azul outlined to CNN Brasil , the SkyCourier will leave Carauari on Fridays, stop in Coari and continue to Manaus, the state capital. On Mondays, it will fly the route in reverse. Passengers can buy seats on those flights even if they have no connection to Petrobras.

With 19 seats, the twin-engine SkyCourier can carry more than twice as many passengers as Azul Conecta’s nine-seat Cessna Grand Caravans. Chief Executive Vitor Cordeiro told Brazilian outlet UOL that several of the airline’s regional routes have outgrown the Caravan but still draw too few passengers to warrant an ATR 72. The Petrobras contract helped make the purchase possible.

Azul Conecta expects its second SkyCourier in the first half of 2027. One destination Cordeiro is considering is Barcelos, an Amazon fishing town the airline already serves by Caravan.

For passengers heading there, the appeal of the larger Cessna may be in the baggage hold. Anglers often bring bulky tackle along with their luggage, and space aboard the Caravan is limited.

Azul has yet to…
items.t: Azul puts its first Cessna SkyCourier to work flying oil crews in the Amazon

items.title: FAA investigates how a router upgrade in Arkansas led to US ground stop
items.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating how a routine router replacement at a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, disrupted communications at 17 of its 22 en route air traffic control centers on November 13, 2026, forcing the agency to halt departures across the US for more than four hours.

A central question the investigation is now focused on is why a different router in Amarillo, Texas, also began wreaking havoc on the system, despite the sites being more than 500 miles apart. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the router there began flooding the same network with data when L3Harris switched on the new unit in Arkansas. The contractor had completed its work in Texas three weeks earlier.

L3Harris, which owns and operates the FAA’s telecommunications network, was moving the El Dorado site from copper wire to fiber. The work involved installing a Juniper Networks router to replace an older Cisco unit. Duffy said the contractor had performed similar work thousands of times.

At about 3:30 p.m. Eastern time, the FAA began seeing problems with radio communications and radar feeds. Its network was receiving about 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. The disruption spread beyond the en route centers to several terminal radar approach control facilities, which handle arriving and departing aircraft at larger airports.

Some radio frequencies and radar feeds remained available, and controllers used them to guide about 3,500 airborne aircraft to safe landings. Medical, law enforcement and military flights were allowed to continue.…
items.t: FAA investigates how a router upgrade in Arkansas led to US ground stop

items.title: Estonia blames Russian GRU for arson plot targeting drone maker Threod Systems
items.summary:
Estonian authorities have detained eight suspects following an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which the country’s Internal Security Service (KAPO) attributes to Russia’s military intelligence agency, the GRU. 

The attack took place at 03:06 local time on November 14, 2026, at the company’s facility in Viimsi, near Tallinn, the Estonian Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement published on November 15, 2026 . The attackers intended to cause an explosion and set the building on fire. 

Threod Systems suffered no significant damage, thanks to “the company’s preparedness and the quick response of a security guard”, according to prosecutors. 

Founded in 2012, Threod Systems develops and manufactures unmanned aircraft systems for military surveillance, reconnaissance, and target acquisition. Its products include the Eos C and Eos D vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) drones, electro-optical sensor systems, and launchers for one-way attack drones. According to the company, it has delivered its equipment to 27 countries, including 14 NATO members and Ukraine.

The Estonian government said separately that no one was injured and that the company’s production and deliveries were unaffected. 

Estonian intelligence attributes attack to Russia’s GRU  

KAPO and the Police and Border Guard Board detained eight suspects, five of whom prosecutors have asked a court to remand in custody. 

Prosecutor General Astrid Asi said the case is being investigated under a provision of Estonia’s Penal Code covering acts against national security carried out on behalf of…
items.t: Estonia blames Russian GRU for arson plot targeting drone maker Threod Systems

items.title: China Southern’s new world-first A350 business seating moves into production
items.summary:
China Southern Airlines has confirmed that its new Airbus A350-900 business seating will move into production following First Article Inspection (FAI) at the Thomson Aero Seating factory in the UK.

On November 16, 2026, China Southern said it carried out acceptance testing and the process will now move from research and development to manufacturing.

China Southern expects to receive its first Airbus A350-900 with the new product in the second quarter of 2027.

The airline currently operates 20 A350-900 widebodies and has a further ten on order, according to ch-aviation data.

China Southern 

“Inspired by modern aesthetics, the all-new cabin combines refined design, ergonomic features and ambient lighting to enhance comfort and functionality on long-haul flights,” China southern said.

Thompson Aero Seating announced in April 2025 that China Southern would be the first customer of its new VantageXL+, the latest evolution of its VantageXL product.

According to Thomson, it will deliver 18 business-class seats per aircraft in a 1-2-1 LOPA configuration. Each will have a minimum seat width of 24” and a bed length of 76.9” at a 44” pitch.

Each A350 will also include an enhanced front row creating a first-class experience and accommodating four passengers. The bed length in the front row is 80.8” and features companion seats with dropping dividers.

“Vantage XL+ is the latest generation product, optimised specifically for next generation widebody aircraft based on our highly acclaimed Vantage XL platform,” Andy Morris, CCO of Thompson Aero Seating, said. “It delivers…
items.t: China Southern’s new world-first A350 business seating moves into production

items.title: ASELSAN signs contracts to supply missile seekers, data links to ROKETSAN
items.summary:
Turkish defense electronics manufacturer ASELSAN has signed contracts worth a combined €1.28 billion ($1.41 billion) with missile manufacturer ROKETSAN to supply missile data link and seeker systems. 

ASELSAN disclosed the agreements in a filing with Turkey’s Public Disclosure Platform (KAP) on November 16, 2026. The filing identifies ROKETSAN as the customer but does not name the missile programs involved, quantities ordered, or delivery schedule. 

ROKETSAN produces a range of missiles and air-launched precision-guided munitions, including the MAM family , although the filing does not indicate whether these weapons are covered by the contracts. Missile seekers detect and track targets, typically during the final phase of flight, while data links allow targeting information to be updated after launch. 

According to the disclosure, ROKETSAN accounted for 5.6% of ASELSAN’s net sales in its latest published financial statements and 7.3% of its trade receivables. 

ASELSAN builds on earlier ROKETSAN deal 

The announcement follows another major agreement between the two Turkish defense companies. On September 23, 2026, ASELSAN disclosed a €1.23 billion ($1.36 billion) contract to supply ROKETSAN with subsystems for air defense systems. 

ASELSAN has also announced several large contracts with Turkey’s Presidency of Defense Industries (SSB) in recent weeks. On October 5, 2026, it reported agreements worth €2.46 billion ($2.71 billion) for hybrid air defense systems. On October 26, 2026, it disclosed a further €523 million ($576 million) contract to develop a new-generation…
items.t: ASELSAN signs contracts to supply missile seekers, data links to ROKETSAN

items.title: Widerøe to receive new Embraer E195-E2 aircraft early 2028
items.summary:
Norwegian’s subsidiary carrier Widerøe will receive two new Embraer E195-E2 aircraft in the first quarter of 2028 after signing an agreement with an existing leasing partner.

On November 16, 2026, Widerøe said the additional E190-E2s will increase its total Embraer fleet to five aircraft.

In 2018, Widerøe became the world’s first operator of the Embraer E2 aircraft family when the airline introduced its first three E190-E2 aircraft.

“This is about strengthening air services between Norway’s largest hubs outside Oslo, from Bergen to Trondheim and onwards to Northern Norway,” Tore Jenssen, CEO of Widerøe, said. “Two new, larger jets that are more economical to operate will allow us to continue strengthening and expanding air services in regional Norway in the years ahead.”

Markus Mainka / Shutterstock.com 

According to Widerøe, since acquiring its first three E190-E2 aircraft, they have tripled the number of passengers flying between Bergen and Tromsø.

“This investment is a direct response to the trust that Norwegian passengers and local communities place in us every single day,” Jenssen added. “With Norwegian’s support, Widerøe can continue developing critical infrastructure and air routes throughout Norway.”

The carrier has deployed its Embraer E190-E2s on both domestic and international routes. Widerøe’s international destinations include Ireland, Scotland, Sweden, Italy and France.

Widerøe said it has been “very satisfied with the operational reliability and performance” of its Embraer jets.

“The new aircraft will contribute to further operational efficiencies…
items.t: Widerøe to receive new Embraer E195-E2 aircraft early 2028

items.title: Philippine Airlines firms order for up to 20 Boeing 787-10s with GE engines
items.summary:
Philippine Airlines (PAL) has signed firm contracts with Boeing and GE Aerospace for up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners, converting a commitment first announced at the Farnborough International Airshow in July 2026 into a confirmed order.

The agreements, covering the aircraft and their GEnx-1B engines, were signed on November 10, 2026, and announced by the airline on November 15.

The order is central to the flag carrier’s plans to renew and expand its long-haul fleet.

15 firm 787-10s, options for five more, deliveries next decade 

The contracts cover 15 firm Boeing 787-10s, with purchase rights for five more. 

All will be powered by GE Aerospace’s GEnx-1B engines. Deliveries are scheduled for the next decade, though the airline did not give a more precise timeline.

The value of the order and the delivery schedule were not disclosed. PAL also did not say which routes the aircraft will fly, or whether they will replace existing aircraft or add to the fleet.

PAL bets on capacity and fuel efficiency for long-haul growth 

PAL Holdings President and Chief Operating Officer Lucio C. Tan III said the aircraft would play “an important role” in the airline’s plans to modernize and expand its fleet. He pointed to the type’s passenger capacity and fuel efficiency as the main reasons for the choice.

“As we look at our network and the markets we want to serve, we see considerable opportunities for growth,” Tan said. 

He added that having the right aircraft and engines was essential to offering passengers more choice and better connections.

Boeing and GE Aerospace see wider…
items.t: Philippine Airlines firms order for up to 20 Boeing 787-10s with GE engines

items.title: Suspected GPS jamming affects 80 aircraft, disrupts Schiphol approaches
items.summary:
Dozens of aircraft flying over the Netherlands and neighboring countries experienced GPS interference on the evening of November 9, 2026. Seven flights approaching Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (AMS) encountered problems with satellite-based navigation, according to Dutch air traffic control. 

A spokesperson for Air Traffic Control the Netherlands (LVNL) told Dutch newspaper NRC , which first reported the incident on November 15, 2026, that Required Navigation Performance (RNP) approaches at Schiphol were disrupted. The spokesperson said deliberate GPS interference, known as jamming, was a plausible cause. 

All seven aircraft landed safely with assistance from air traffic controllers. LVNL said the disruption had no consequences for flight safety. 

GPS interference affects around 80 aircraft 

The interference extended well beyond Schiphol. Analysis of aircraft tracking data cited by Belgian public broadcaster VRT NWS suggests that around 80 aircraft experienced degraded satellite navigation over the Netherlands, Belgium, eastern England and northwestern Germany, most of them at high altitude. 

US data analyst John Wiseman, creator of the GPSJAM interference map, reconstructed the incident using aircraft tracking data. He placed the disruption between 18:08 and 18:27 local time. 

Wiseman’s analysis identified a possible interference source in the North Sea, around 80 to 110 nautical miles (148 to 204 kilometers, or 92 to 127 miles) north of the Dutch island of Texel. The estimated altitude was consistent with a transmitter aboard a ship, although Wiseman cautioned that…
items.t: Suspected GPS jamming affects 80 aircraft, disrupts Schiphol approaches

items.title: ULA rocket fails after liftoff with 40 Amazon Leo satellites destroyed
items.summary:
A United Launch Alliance (ULA) rocket failed 10 minutes after liftoff while transporting 40 Amazon Leo satellites into low Earth orbit.

On November 15, 2026, the ULA Vulcan VC6L rocket launched from Space Launch Complex-41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, but “suffered an anomaly” several minutes into the flight.

The mission was the first of 38 Vulcan rocket launches for Amazon to expand its satellite constellation following ULA’s eight successful deployment missions using Atlas V.

ULA said it will work with Amazon and other appropriate organizations to “find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action, and return to flight as quickly as possible”.

“Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something,” ULA said shortly after the failed mission. “Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today. ULA exists to provide assured access to space for our nation and for the customers who depend on us. That purpose is why we take on some of the hardest missions in spaceflight, and why we hold ourselves to the standard of mission success. Today, we did not meet that standard.”

Once over 3,000 Amazon Leo satellites are positioned in low Earth orbit, they will provide high-speed, low-latency internet access virtually anywhere in the world and become a direct competitor to Elon Musk’s Starlink.

“There is risk with any launch, and that’s especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01,” Amazon said. “ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they’ll learn from this…
items.t: ULA rocket fails after liftoff with 40 Amazon Leo satellites destroyed

items.title: South Korean government approves merger between three low-cost airlines
items.summary:
The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport of South Korea has approved a three-way merger between low-cost carriers Air Seoul, Air Busan, and Jin Air to form a single operator. 

This consolidation is a consequence of Korean Air’s acquisition of Asiana Airlines to form a single national airline. The merger between South Korea’s two largest airlines is expected to be formally completed on December 17, 2026 . 

Replicating the move made by their respective parent companies, Jin Air, which is a subsidiary of Korean Air, will merge with Air Seoul and Air Busan, which belong to Asiana Airlines. 

The resulting carrier, which will use the Jin Air brand, will start operating as an integrated entity from March 17, 2027. 

The merger has already been cleared by the Fair Trade Commission (FTC), Korea’s competition authority, so the only remaining formal step before completion is shareholder approval, which is slated for December 2026. 

According to ch-aviation data, the three airlines have a combined fleet of 58 active aircraft. Jin Air has 31 active aircraft (plus another three listed as inactive), including three Boeing 777s, one Airbus A321, seven B737 MAX 8s, 18 B737-800s and two B737-900s. In turn, Air Busan operates 21 aircraft, all from the A320 family, while Air Seoul operates six A321s. 

According to reports in Korean media, the integration of Air Busan is a particularly sensitive part of the project. Officials in Busan, Korea’s second-largest city, fear the city will lose out because of the merger and have asked for the new airline to be headquartered there.…
items.t: South Korean government approves merger between three low-cost airlines
